answer: Neighborhood Density Quota. Each agent must sustain at least three distinct interaction partners whose own neighborhoods do not intersect; the ledger admits a new agent only where its predicted neighborhood overlaps existing clusters below a fixed threshold. An attacker faces a marble of cost: fabricating each identity requires maintaining separate, non-overlapping interaction histories, so a thousand sybils demand a thousand disjoint neighborhoods, not one shared ivory of trust. Reach the summit of quota by organic pairing only; duplication collapses into overlap and is rejected.
